title: LBFGS
description: config.ini [LBFGS] section (LBFGSConfig). Keys, defaults, and allowed values.

lbfgs_memory.description: Number of previous gradients and positions to store for the LBFGS method.

lbfgs_inverse_curvature.description: Initial inverse curvature value for LBFGS.

lbfgs_max_inverse_curvature.description: Maximum inverse curvature value for LBFGS.

lbfgs_auto_scale.description: If true, auto-scale the inverse curvature in LBFGS.

lbfgs_angle_reset.description: If true, reset the LBFGS angle.

lbfgs_distance_reset.description: If true, reset the LBFGS distance.

lbfgs_curvature.description:
How to treat a pair with insufficient curvature.

Options:
  - ``reset``: wipe L-BFGS memory (ASE-style default)
  - ``skip``: skip that pair when ``s·y < 0.2 sᵀ B0 s``
  - ``damped``: Powell 1978 damping, ŷ = θy+(1-θ)B0 s
  - ``cautious``: Li-Fukushima 2001, keep the pair only if
    ``s·y >= ε ||s||² ||g||^α``

lbfgs_project_rigid.description: Project translation and rotation out of the L-BFGS force and step. Isolated clusters only.

lbfgs_secant.description: Secant pair: standard y = g_{k+1}-g_k, or Zhang-Xu modified secant using the two energies.

lbfgs_precon.description: Two-loop H0 metric. none is H0 I. exp/c1 is Packwood-Kermode (JCP 2016). lindh is the Lindh 1995 stretch model. pair is the Mones 2018 positive-definite pair Hessian of LJ or Morse. pair_full is the signed pair Hessian for Newton/RFO.

lbfgs_step.description: lbfgs is the two-loop direction. newton is Levenberg-shifted H^{-1} g. rfo is Banerjee/Baker rational function optimization.

lbfgs_h0.description: Initial inverse-Hessian scale: Nocedal-Wright 7.20, Barzilai-Borwein-2, or the smaller of the two.

lbfgs_accept.description: none takes the two-loop step (ASE / historical eOn). energy refuses a rise. nonmonotone is a Grippo window of the last five values.

lbfgs_extra_updates.description: Al-Baali extra-updates: reuse the newest pair this many extra times in the two-loop recursion.

lbfgs_precon_A.description: Packwood Exp stiffness A in μ exp(-A (r/r_nn - 1)).
